name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text:
Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It’s the fastest way to boost output quality without slowing down generation—depth maps let it sharpen edges and textures where they matter most, giving a visible lift in detail for minimal compute cost. The trade-off is extra VRAM usage, but it’s under 2GB and runs on the same GPU we already dedicate to EXCAVA.

The artifact: a ComfyUI workflow file with the upscaler node pre-wired and tested on a sample frame.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—faces blur worse under depth maps because skin texture lacks sharp depth cues. Instead, test RealVisXL’s face-detail preset first; it’s a 0.5%+ lift with zero pipeline risk. Settle it by running a blind A/B on 50 samples—faces only—measuring SSIM and a human “recognizable” score.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s face-detail preset to EXCAVA’s pipeline. Faces are the hardest part to sharpen with depth maps, and RealVisXL’s preset is built to preserve skin texture and micro-details without extra compute—it’s a direct 0.5%+ lift on the metric that matters most. The trade-off is zero pipeline risk but limited scope: this won’t help non-face elements, so we’ll still need the depth-aware upscaler later for backgrounds and objects.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face preset risks style drift—faces may look over-smoothed or waxy under EXCAVA’s existing pipeline, killing consistency. Test SDXL-Lightning’s face-detail LoRA instead; it’s a 0.5%+ lift with no style shift and settles the argument with a blind A/B on 50 face-only samples, measuring both fidelity and prompt adherence.
